# Egami: guide for coding agents

Egami is a fully managed 2D imaging library for .NET 10: it loads, edits and saves images, with no native code and no
third-party dependencies. This package holds rasters, pixel types, the image formats, operations, color management and
metadata. Drawing, fonts, SVG, CSS, metafiles, barcodes, HEIC, the extra formats and video are separate packages that build on it.

Namespaces: `Egami` (rasters, `EgamiContext`), `Egami.Pixels` (pixel types), `Egami.Formats` and `Egami.Formats.<Format>`
(readers, writers and their options), `Egami.Operations` (what `Apply` and `Derive` take), `Egami.Metadata`.

## Egami's vocabulary

Egami has its own names. Use them, not names from other imaging libraries: Egami has no `Image` type, no `Mutate` or `Clone`
and no `Configuration`.

- `Raster` and `Raster<TPixel>` hold an image; `TPixel` is a pixel type such as `Rgba8`, `Rgb8`, `Gray8`, `Bgra8` or `RgbaF32`
  (namespace `Egami.Pixels`). `Raster.Load` returns the type that fits the file; `Raster.Load<Rgba8>` converts while decoding.
- `Raster.Probe` reads a file's size, format and orientation without decoding it.
- `Apply(ops => ...)` changes a raster in place through a chain of operations; `Derive(ops => ...)` returns a new raster.
  `As<TPixel>()` converts to a new raster and `Copy()` duplicates one.
- `Save(path)` picks the writer from the extension; `Save(stream, format, options)` names it. Loading always detects the format
  from the bytes, never from the extension.
- `EgamiContext` holds the settings, `SafetyLimits`, thread count and registered formats a call uses. It is immutable: change
  it with `with`, and pass it to `Load` or `Probe`, or make it the default once at startup with `EgamiContext.SetDefault`.
- Every `Raster` owns pooled pixel memory: dispose it, best with `using`. `Derive`, `As` and `Load` return new rasters that you
  dispose too.

## Entry points

- `Raster.Load`, `Raster.LoadAsync`, `Raster.Probe`: from a path, a stream or bytes, with an optional `EgamiContext` and
  `ReaderOptions`.
- `Raster.Create<TPixel>(width, height, fill)`: a new image.
- `raster.Apply(ops => ...)` and `raster.Derive(ops => ...)`: `Fit`, `Resize`, `Crop`, `AutoOrient`, `Grayscale`, `Blur`,
  `Sharpen`, `Saturation` and the other operations, chained.
- `raster.Row(y)`: one row of pixels as a `Span<TPixel>`, for your own pixel loops.
- `raster.Save`, `raster.SaveAsync`: by extension, or with a `FormatInfo` such as `JpegFormat.Info` and writer options such as
  `JpegWriterOptions`.
- `Raster.Transcode(input, output, ops => ...)`: load, edit and save a large file without holding the whole image.

## Samples

Load, make a thumbnail and save:

```csharp
// Load in the pixel type that best fits the file (here Rgba8: this PNG stores alpha).
using Raster image = Raster.Load("duck.png");
Console.WriteLine($"{image.Width} × {image.Height}, {image.Layout.ChannelOrder}");

// Make a thumbnail that fits 200 × 200, keeping the aspect ratio, and save it as JPEG.
image.Apply(ops => ops.Fit(200, 200));
image.Save("duck-small.jpg");
```

Work in a pixel type you choose:

```csharp
// Decode straight into the type you want to work in.
using Raster<Rgba8> rgba = Raster.Load<Rgba8>("duck.png");

// Pixels are a row at a time: each row is a Span<Rgba8>.
for (int y = 0; y < rgba.Height; y++)
{
    Span<Rgba8> row = rgba.Row(y);
    for (int x = 0; x < row.Length; x++)
    {
        row[x].A = 128;
    }
}

// Convert a whole raster; the result is a new raster you dispose too.
using Raster<Gray8> gray = rgba.As<Gray8>();
gray.Save("duck-gray.png");
```

Choose the output format and its options:

```csharp
// Save(path) picks the writer from the file extension...
image.Save("duck-copy.qoi");

// ...or name the format, with its options.
using FileStream output = File.Create("duck-q90.jpg");
image.Save(output, Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegFormat.Info, new Egami.Formats.Jpeg.JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 90 });

// Loading never looks at the extension: the format is detected from the first bytes.
RasterInfo info = Raster.Probe("duck.png");
Console.WriteLine(info.Format.Name);   // PNG
```

A photo thumbnail: smallest JPEG decode, upright, fitted:

```csharp
// Decode at the smallest JPEG scale that still covers 400 × 400, turn it upright, fit it, and save at quality 80.
using Raster photo = Raster.Load("sideways.jpg", options: new ReaderOptions { MinimumSize = new Size(400, 400) });
photo.Apply(ops => ops.AutoOrient().Fit(400, 400, enlarge: false));
photo.Save("thumb.jpg", new JpegWriterOptions { Quality = 80, StripMetadata = true });
```

Files from users: probe first, with limits:

```csharp
EgamiContext strict = EgamiContext.Default with
{
    Limits = SafetyLimits.Default with { MaxPixels = 25_000_000, MaxTotalBytes = 256L * 1024 * 1024 },
};

try
{
    // Read the header first: cheap, and it rejects what you do not want before any pixel memory is used.
    RasterInfo info = Raster.Probe(upload, strict);
    if (info.Width > 8000 || info.Height > 8000)
    {
        throw new InvalidDataException("Too large.");
    }

    using Raster image = Raster.Load(upload, strict, new ReaderOptions { Recovery = RecoveryMode.Strict });
    Console.WriteLine($"{info.Format.Name} {image.Width} × {image.Height}");
}
catch (UnsupportedFormatException)
{
    Console.WriteLine("Not an image format we accept.");
}
catch (LimitExceededException e)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Over the {e.LimitName} limit.");
}
catch (CorruptDataException e)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Damaged at byte {e.Offset}.");
}
```

Many files at once:

```csharp
// Convert a folder of images to QOI, a few at a time. Each image runs on one thread, so the files run side by side.
EgamiContext oneThread = EgamiContext.Default with { MaxParallelism = 1 };
Directory.CreateDirectory("out");
Parallel.ForEach(Directory.GetFiles("in"), new ParallelOptions { MaxDegreeOfParallelism = 4 }, path =>
{
    try
    {
        using Raster image = Raster.Load(path, oneThread);
        image.Save(Path.Combine("out", Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension(path) + ".qoi"));
    }
    catch (EgamiException e)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{path}: {e.Message}");
    }
});
```

## Common mistakes

- Not disposing rasters. Pixel memory is pooled, so a raster left to the garbage collector holds its memory until then. Put
  `using` on every `Load`, `Create`, `Derive`, `As` and `Copy` result.
- Expecting `Apply` to return a new image. `Apply` changes the raster it is called on; use `Derive` to keep the original.
- Forgetting `AutoOrient()` on photos. Camera JPEGs are often stored sideways with an Exif orientation; `Raster.Probe` reports
  it in `Orientation`.
- Resizing with both sizes when the aspect ratio should stay: `Fit(w, h)` keeps it inside a box, `Resize(w, 0)` keeps it from
  one side, `Resize(w, h)` stretches.
- Running many images in parallel with the default context. Each operation already uses several threads; when you run files
  side by side, give each a context with `MaxParallelism = 1`.
- Loading untrusted files without limits. Probe first and pass an `EgamiContext` with `SafetyLimits`; catch
  `UnsupportedFormatException`, `LimitExceededException` and `CorruptDataException` (all are `EgamiException`).
- Expecting HEIC, SVG, PCX and similar formats to load out of the box. HEIC needs Egami.Heic (`WithHeic()`), SVG needs Egami.Svg
  (`WithFormat(SvgFormat.Info)`), PCX, SGI and the other rare formats need Egami.Formats.Extended (`WithExtendedFormats()`).
